name: Can I demolish a pool if there is a spa attached to it?

mainEntity.name: How does pool demolition change when there is an attached spa, hot tub, or raised water feature?
mainEntity.text: How does pool demolition change when there is an attached spa, hot tub, or raised water feature?

acceptedAnswer.text: An attached spa or raised water feature usually makes the project more complex because it may have its own plumbing, electrical, and masonry structure. In some cases, it can be demolished at the same time as the pool shell. In others, it needs separate removal and backfill work. The contractor should inspect how the spa ties into the pool deck, circulation system, and electrical service before quoting the job. Homeowners should ask whether spa demolition is included in the base price and whether any raised walls, coping, or equipment pad work will add cost. If the spa is part of a larger backyard layout, this is also a good time to think about how the finished grade should look after removal.
acceptedAnswer.description: An attached spa or hot tub usually adds demolition time and cost because it may have separate plumbing, electrical, and structural components. The contractor should inspect whether it can be removed with the pool or needs separate demolition.
